video.agency.evidence: [沙王·codex] 图1第4行第4–7格（6.75、7.00、7.25、7.50秒），我在近敌包围中持续抬身、高举双刃，未见明确的压低护头或受击震身反应。按规格6–7.5秒这一拍，我应硬扛抽打并持续完成起伏蓄力；这些格子无法确认我是在主动蓄力承伤，还是举刃停等，依要求判fail。；[树人·claude] Speaking as the treant: in 0–1.5 s (frames 0.000–1.500) all four of us charge in from the four sides, and by 1.5 s we are right next to it. That part is fine. Through 1.75–6.0 s we surround it and raise our branch-arms, and in most frames the arm poses change, so we look like we keep swinging rather than standing idle. But in the 6.75 s, 7.0 s, 7.25 s and 7.5 s frames, while it rears up with both blades over its head to charge, the treants on its left and right stay almost exactly where they were. They stand upright 2–3 m away and their arm poses barely change across the four frames. I can't see any pounce or strike on its shell. Per the spec, a treant would use this charge-up to keep jumping in and hitting it; here they stand and wait, which reads as idle waiting. Also, I can't confirm from the thumbnails that bark flips open and wood chips fly when the blades hit us in 1.5–6 s, so I can't tell whether getting hit draws any reaction. The flailing in 8.0–9.75 s and lying down from 10.0 s on are covered by the control and death exceptions.

video.gaze.evidence: [沙王·codex] 图1第2–3行（2.00–5.75秒），交手时我的头部较小，且受甲盖、前肢及近身树人遮挡，无法逐格确认头朝向是否跟随当前出手与来袭对象；第4行第4–7格（6.75–7.50秒）也无法确认我是否盯着身前地面与最近的树人。未能确认持续有效视线，依要求判fail。；[树人·claude] Speaking as the treant: in 0–1.5 s (frames 0.000–1.500) all four treants' trunks and heads face the scorpion in the center as they charge. In 1.75–6.0 s every treant has its front turned inward toward it, and the ones nearest the camera have their backs to the camera, so their heads face it. In 6.0–7.5 s the treants on both sides still have their heads toward its body. They are being thrown around from 7.75 s on and lying dead in the debris from about 10.0 s on, and those frames are exempt. In no frame does a treant raise its head to the sky or turn to look at the camera. Caveat: the eye sockets are too small to make out in the thumbnails, so this call is based on head and trunk direction.

video.readability.evidence: [audience·claude] Some of it reads clearly. A giant scorpion stands in the middle of a ring of brown, tree-like humanoid creatures (grid 0.000–7.500). It raises both claws at 5.250–5.500 and again at 6.750–7.500. At 7.750 a yellow glowing ring appears on the ground at its feet. From 8.000 to 10.500 yellow shockwave rings spread outward with dust and flying rocks, and the creatures around it are thrown up and outward (clearest at 8.500–9.750). So who cast the skill (the scorpion) and who it hit (the surrounding creatures) are readable. Three things are uncertain, so this is a fail: (1) The result is not readable. From 10.750 to 14.750 the frame is covered in brown haze. The creatures left on the ground are small dark brown clumps that look almost the same as the rocks and soil around them. A first-time viewer cannot tell whether they are dead, knocked down, or gone, and there is no clear defeat signal such as bodies breaking apart, fading out, or a death effect. A few shapes at 12.000–14.750 even look like they might still be standing. (2) It is not clear what triggered the skill. The claws go up at 7.500 and the light appears at 7.750, but you cannot see whether the claws or the tail struck the ground. The glow starts off to the front-left of the scorpion, not clearly under its claws. (3) In the first half (0.000–4.750) the creatures and the scorpion overlap in brown on brown. You cannot tell who is attacking whom, and this stretch makes up half the clip with no readable story beat. Also, the ground in the background suddenly turns green at 8.000–9.000, so the scene seems to change, which adds confusion. In short, a viewer can say 'the scorpion blasted the creatures away with a shockwave', but cannot say what state the enemies end up in.
